advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Synchronize the 'during' os.environ snapshot loop with live worker execution (e.g. a second barrier / an in-flight signal) so the byte-equality check demonstrably overlaps concurrent projection.
evidence: tests/unit/test_child_env_concurrency.py:90: `barrier.wait()  # release all workers at once for maximum contention`
tests/unit/test_child_env_concurrency.py:92: `# Assert the global environment is unmutated WHILE the operations run.`

The worker body (lines 61-85) is pure in-memory dict construction via project_child_env, which src/rebar/_child_env.py:136 shows never touches os.environ; nothing gates worker completion against the 50-iteration snapshot loop, so 'WHILE the operations run' overlap is not guaranteed.
advisory.finding: The 'during' os.environ non-mutation assertion is not synchronized with worker execution: the main thread releases the barrier then runs a fixed 50-iteration snapshot loop, but workers perform only pure in-memory dict work that can complete before or independently of that loop, so the loop may run entirely after the workers finish and does not actually observe os.environ 'during' concurrent projection as the docstring/commit claim.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unused `stop` Event and its per-iteration `stop.is_set()` guard, or actually set `stop` before joining so it performs a real early-exit.
evidence: `stop.set()` runs only after the join loop completes (per diff: the join loop precedes `stop.set()`), so no worker is still looping when it is set.
advisory.finding: The `stop` threading.Event is effectively dead code: workers check `if stop.is_set(): return` at the top of each loop iteration, but `stop.set()` is only called after every worker thread has already been joined, so the guard can never fire during the run and adds no early-exit behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the owning concurrency oracle live teeth for cross-operation credential observation (e.g. have some workers omit their own overlay so a leaked sibling/ambient value would actually surface), instead of an overlay that deterministically overwrites the key and makes the leak checks unreachable.
evidence: Owning worker always passes overlay={"JIRA_API_TOKEN": my_token} (line 68), and source applies it unconditionally: src/rebar/_child_env.py:140-141 `if relationship == "owning" and overlay is not None: result.update(overlay)`
Therefore env["JIRA_API_TOKEN"] is ALWAYS my_token; the check at line 71 (`!= my_token`) subsumes all outcomes and returns first

Line 75 `if env.get("JIRA_API_TOKEN") == "AMBIENT-SENTINEL-MUST-NOT-LEAK"` can never be True (overlay forces my_token), and line 79 `if env["JIRA_API_TOKEN"] in other_tokens` can never be True — both are unreachable
Regression blindness: a defect that let a sibling's credential or the ambient sentinel be observed by an owning child would still be overwritten by the overlay in this test, so the oracle stays green
advisory.finding: In the owning-projection concurrency test, the cross-operation-credential and ambient-sentinel-leak assertions are unreachable dead code, so the test cannot detect a regression in AC4's core 'no cross-operation credential observation' behavior for owning children.
scenarios: A future regression where owning projection stops applying the overlay or leaks a sibling's ambient value under contention would not be caught by this test's owning oracle.
